entries.clue: Identify American in river (5)

blocks.note: to tag something is to label or identify it

annotation.surface: Someone is asked to pick out an American swimming in a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container instruction, but it only joins the wordplay to the definition. The Tagus flows through Spain and Portugal to Lisbon.
annotation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula.

entries.clue: Idiot limits chemical tests (10)

blocks.note: tit is British slang for a fool
rations = fixed limits on what you may have

annotation.surface: A fool puts a cap on how much lab testing can be done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Limits' reads as a verb in the surface but is a plural noun here. 'Tit' as an insult is everyday British slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: A titration measures a solution's concentration by adding a reagent until a reaction completes: a chemical test.

entries.clue: Great! Promotion for old man (7)

annotation.surface: Someone cheers at news of a job promotion for their elderly father.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' pretends to be a rise at work; it is advertising.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Old man' is a familiar term for a grandfather or any elderly man.

entries.clue: Infected with cold in Alabama, is dubious (9)

indicatorNotes.with: SEPTIC is 'with' the C inside it
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the cold inside the word for infected, so C sits within SEPTIC

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
AL is the postal code for Alabama

annotation.surface: A news line about someone in Alabama who caught a chill and doubts the diagnosis.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after Alabama makes 'is dubious' look like a comment on the patient; 'is' only links, and US state postal codes are standard crossword currency.
annotation.definitionFit: Sceptical and dubious both mean doubtful, unconvinced.

entries.clue: Give alcohol to legendary director taking clothes off behind screens (9)

indicatorNotes.taking clothes off: stripping the director's outer letters, as if undressing him
indicatorNotes.screens: LATE screens, or hides, the stripped name inside it

blocks.note: Stanley KUBRICK with his first and last letters stripped

annotation.surface: A famous film director is plied with drink and strips off behind the screens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Screens' looks like cinema screens to go with the director; it is the containment verb. To lubricate someone is slang for getting them drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Informally, to lubricate someone is to ply them with alcohol.

entries.clue: Replenishment of drink briefly boosted long-term prisoner (5)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.boosted: in a down clue, raised upward, so read bottom to top

blocks.note: REFILL with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A top-up of drink cheers up a man serving a long sentence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boosted' seems to say the drink lifted the prisoner's spirits; in a down clue it sends the letters upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A lifer is someone serving a life sentence.

entries.clue: Confidence about oddly absurd artwork that's outstanding (3-6)

indicatorNotes.about: BELIEF goes around the other letters
indicatorNotes.oddly: take the odd-numbered letters: A, S, R

blocks.note: A, S, R are letters 1, 3 and 5 of ABSURD

annotation.surface: Someone has faith in a ridiculous piece of art that others call outstanding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to be praise, but it is literal: a bas-relief is carving that stands out slightly from its background.
annotation.definitionFit: A bas-relief is a sculpture raised a little from a flat surface, so it literally stands out.

entries.clue: Chemical compound in victim identified (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the next words

annotation.surface: A poison is found in the body once the victim has been named.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a forensic report, which keeps the eye on the victim rather than the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An imide is an organic compound with two acyl groups bonded to nitrogen.

entries.clue: Visiting a river in East Anglia with a large dry patch (7)

annotation.surface: A tourist on an East Anglian river notices a parched stretch of bank.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'large dry patch' seems to be on the English riverbank; it is a whole desert in Chile, among the driest places on Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: The Atacama is a vast desert in northern Chile, famously almost rainless.

entries.clue: Rugby game without wingers is flat (4)

indicatorNotes.without wingers: wingers play on the edges, so drop the outer letters

blocks.note: SEVENS minus its first and last S

annotation.surface: A rugby match with no wide players turns out dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wingers' are genuine rugby positions on the flanks, which is exactly why they mean the word's outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Flat and even both describe a level surface.

entries.clue: Staff redo badly written compromises (5-4)

indicatorNotes.badly written: the letters are set down wrongly, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Employees must rewrite a poorly drafted agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'redo' sit together like a workplace instruction, which hides that they are the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A trade-off is a compromise where one gain is accepted for another loss.

entries.clue: One elderly relative beginning to emerge, senseless (5)

annotation.surface: An aged relative comes round after being knocked out.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone regaining consciousness, but 'senseless' is the definition meaning silly, not unconscious.
annotation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, without sense.

entries.clue: Read regulation out for official supervising public accounts (7,7)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A rule is read aloud for the benefit of a senior government auditor.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the kind of thing an auditor-general does, so the fodder looks like part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: An auditor general is the official who audits government spending.

entries.clue: Detective losing extremely versatile ringleader (10)

indicatorNotes.losing: take letters away from the detective
indicatorNotes.extremely: use only the extreme, outer letters of 'versatile'

blocks.note: V and E, the ends of versatile, are removed

annotation.surface: A police force loses a very flexible detective who led a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely versatile' reads as high praise; it means just the two end letters, V and E.
annotation.definitionFit: An instigator stirs up trouble, the leader behind it.

entries.clue: Encouraged popular Italian leader back to motherland (7)

indicatorNotes.back to: the back, or last letter, of 'motherland'

annotation.surface: A well-liked Italian leader was persuaded to return home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back to motherland' seems to mean a return journey; it points only at the final D.
annotation.definitionFit: To induce someone is to persuade or encourage them.

entries.clue: Online businesswoman Dorothy picked up butterfly (9)

indicatorNotes.picked up: heard, as a radio picks up a signal: go by sound

blocks.note: the comma is a butterfly; COMMER sounds the same in non-rhotic British speech

annotation.surface: A woman named Dorothy who trades online has caught a butterfly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like catching the butterfly in a net. The comma butterfly is named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing.
annotation.definitionFit: A dotcommer works in an internet business; this clue's woman is one.

entries.clue: Fix section of leaking raincoat (7)

indicatorNotes.section of: the answer is a section of the next words

annotation.surface: Someone wants to mend a leaky patch of their raincoat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like a repair, but here it means to make something firmly set.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of setting something firmly, as a habit or a stain is fixed deep in the fibres.

entries.clue: Poisonous individual's extraordinary dig at NATO (5,4)

indicatorNotes.extraordinary: out of the ordinary order, so rearrange

annotation.surface: A spiteful person makes a remarkable jibe at the military alliance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poisonous individual' reads as a nasty person; it is literal. The giant or cane toad secretes toxin from glands behind its eyes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the cane toad's skin glands ooze a toxin that kills pets and predators, so a single one is a poisonous individual.

entries.clue: Hard to abandon charity broadcast after returning short annotation (7)

indicatorNotes.to abandon: to abandon is to walk out on something, so the H walks out of the word
indicatorNotes.returning: then the result goes back the other way

blocks.note: H = hard, as on pencils; it is removed
a telethon is a long TV fundraiser

annotation.surface: It is hard to walk away from a fundraising programme.
annotation.walkthrough: TELETHON loses its H to leave TELETON, which read backwards is the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small note; 'short annotation' stretches it a little toward a brief written note.

entries.clue: In addition, win large drills, and something to keep them in? (7)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
to bag a prize is to win it

annotation.surface: Someone wins some big power drills as well, and wonders where to store them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Them' points back at the drills in the clue, and the question mark flags that a toolbag is one fitting home for them. The clue gives win before large, but L comes first in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A toolbag is a bag for carrying tools such as drills.

entries.clue: Uniform available as quickly as possible (4,3)

blocks.note: out = available, as a newly released book is out

annotation.surface: A shop promises its uniforms can be supplied at top speed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' pretends to be clothing; it is the adjective meaning unvarying.
annotation.definitionFit: Going flat out means going at full speed.

entries.clue: Gold and diamonds enthralling single female, leading to opening (7)

indicatorNotes.enthralling: holding captive, so the outer letters hold the inner ones

annotation.surface: Jewellery captivates an unmarried woman and opens a door for her.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Single female' looks like one phrase for an unmarried woman; it splits into two letters. Or is the heraldic word for gold, and ice is slang for diamonds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: orifice is the formal, often anatomical, word for an opening or vent.

entries.clue: Fine 4-0, with United dispatched, being profligate (4-3-7)

indicatorNotes.dispatched: sent away, so U leaves FOUR

blocks.note: the digit read as a word
U, the abbreviation for United, is removed from FOUR to leave FOR

annotation.surface: A football report: a fine 4-0 win with Manchester United sent packing, and a wasteful display.
annotation.walkthrough: The scoreline reads as a football result, with United as the beaten team; instead the digits are read as words and U, a standard abbreviation in team names, is dropped.
annotation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is idle and worthless, much like a profligate wastrel.

entries.clue: Fear Republican stopping late (5)

indicatorNotes.stopping: R stops, or plugs, the gap inside DEAD

blocks.note: the late = the dead, as in 'the late king'

annotation.surface: Someone is afraid a Republican will stay up too late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late' is the formal sense, deceased.
annotation.definitionFit: Dread and fear are synonyms, as nouns or verbs.

entries.clue: Potentially lousy sex with Trump, initially, in his home city (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the letters go inside the city

blocks.note: it = sex, as in 'up for it'

annotation.surface: A salacious tabloid line about sex with Trump in New York.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' seems to mean dreadful; it is literal, full of lice, and nits are lice eggs. 'His home city' needs Trump as a New Yorker.
annotation.definitionFit: Nitty means infested with nits, so potentially lousy, crawling with lice.

entries.clue: Eye part of Emerald Isle, briefly (4)

indicatorNotes.briefly: cut short: drop the last letter

annotation.surface: A short description of a feature of Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of' seems to signal a hidden word; it belongs to the definition 'Eye part'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain part-for-whole definition: the iris is the coloured ring around the pupil.

entries.clue: Canon hiding billion in cash for Russian (5)

indicatorNotes.hiding: to hide something is to keep it tucked inside, so RULE holds the B within it

blocks.note: a canon is a rule or law

annotation.surface: A camera firm is stashing a billion in Russian money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canon' reads as the camera company; it is a rule. RUBLE is the American spelling of rouble.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: Russians pay in rubles, so it is literally the cash a Russian carries.

entries.clue: Member of The Christians playing modest hit (9)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters play around into a new order

annotation.surface: A member of the 1980s pop band The Christians plays their minor chart success.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'The Christians' look like the Liverpool band; it is just Christians in general, of whom a Methodist is one.
annotation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to a Protestant Christian denomination.

entries.clue: Son matured by eating that woman in Bow's cheese (4,5)

indicatorNotes.eating: AGED BY eats ER, taking it inside

blocks.note: aged = matured, plus BY as printed
'ER is HER without the H, as a Cockney says it

annotation.surface: A son has grown up thanks to eating a local woman's cheese.
annotation.walkthrough: Bow is in the East End of London, where Cockneys drop their H's, so 'her' becomes 'er. Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: this is an English hard cheese from Derbyshire, marbled green with sage.

entries.clue: Dispirited daughter getting behind (5)

annotation.surface: A gloomy daughter is falling behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as lagging; it is the noun, a rear.
annotation.definitionFit: Drear, a poetic form of dreary, means gloomy and dispiriting.
